questions.q: Which two visuals does this lesson say are enough to fully answer the VP's original question?
options: A line chart of ticket count by day and priority, and a matrix table with the exact numbers behind it
A map visual showing tickets by region
A single KPI card showing total tickets for the year
A pie chart of ticket status and a scatter plot of channel versus priority
questions.explain: The line chart shows the shape of the month at a glance; the matrix gives the exact numbers behind it — together they fully answer the original ask.

questions.q: Why does the lesson warn against adding extra visuals or breakdowns the VP didn't ask for, even if they'd be easy to add?
options: Power BI limits reports to exactly two visuals
It's scope creep — the same trap Lesson 1 warned about, just showing up at the end of the project instead of the start
The VP of Support is not allowed to see more than two visuals at once
Extra visuals would break the Snowflake connection
questions.explain: Matching effort to the actual ask applies at presentation time just as much as it did during Lesson 1's requirements clarification.

questions.q: What does this lesson say 'done' actually looks like for this project?
options: The report has the maximum possible number of visuals
The report uses DirectQuery instead of Import
The VP can open the report, find the number they need without help, and trust it because they understand roughly how it's built
The VP never has to click Refresh
questions.explain: A report that looks polished but the stakeholder can't use or trust unaided hasn't actually met the bar this lesson sets.

questions.q: According to the suggested walkthrough, what should come first when presenting the report to the VP?
options: Explaining the full COPY INTO and GRANT statements used to build it
Switching to DirectQuery mode live during the meeting
Asking the VP to write their own DAX formulas
Stating the question the report answers, in the VP's own words
questions.explain: Grounding the walkthrough in the VP's own original question keeps the presentation focused on what they actually asked for.

questions.q: If the VP asks for a new breakdown (say, by support channel) after seeing the report, what does this lesson suggest that means?
options: The entire project needs to be rebuilt from scratch immediately
It's useful information for scoping a follow-up project, not evidence that this project failed
Power BI needs to be reconnected using DirectQuery
The original requirements clarification in Lesson 1 was done incorrectly
questions.explain: A new question that the current report can't answer is real signal for the next piece of scope — not proof the original scoping was wrong.
